evidence: Read find() in the head worktree, internal/memory/search.go lines 100-229. I did not run anything, including tests.

Default path with hybrid off: the dense pool is k, as before, and the mode is ModeDense. The old confidence test used merged[0].Score. When there are no topic hits, merged[0] is the first dense hit, which is the new cosine variable. The topic-hit case is handled earlier in the switch. So default behavior is equivalent.

Hybrid path: confidence uses dense[0].Score, as S5 requires. An empty dense result gives cosine 0, which is low confidence. A dense ErrUnavailable falls back to lexical mode with unknown confidence. A lexical error in hybrid mode is returned, the same way the lexical fallback returns it.
fuse() keeps the dense order on ties because the sort is stable. It keeps at most k results and deduplicates by ID. The pool is never smaller than k, so the pool is at least k when k exceeds 50.
The err variable inside the hybrid case is shadowed. The later check `if err == nil && len(dense) > 0` uses the outer dense error, which is correct.
mc-bench rejects -hybrid together with -lexical. The Setup refactor updates all RunQuestion callers in the diff, including the tests. mc-accept sets hybrid only on the dense service.
Hit.Score is an RRF score in hybrid mode. mc-accept documents this in its flag text, and the mode is opt-in. I found no consumer of the score that this commit breaks.
